decisions.executionNote: Approach the inner left and right supports with open grippers, raising elbows gradually and pitching wrists downward. Geometry estimated from calibrated RGB.
Align both grippers over the inner white supports and descend to a cautious pregrasp, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Close around both aligned supports, then make a small test lift. Retention will be judged from the next RGB views.
Both supports appear retained. Lift clear and translate inward to a symmetric base pair, keeping the blocks upright.
Lower the symmetric base supports to the table and release gently without rotating them.
Withdraw upward from the released supports, then move outward and begin orienting both wrists for a two-ended lower-board grasp.
Complete inward-facing wrist alignment and approach above the two ends of the long lower board. Both base supports appear upright and symmetric.
Descend to the lower board, close both end grasps, then test-lift together while keeping the board level.
Lift the long board vertically with synchronized closed grippers and pause to verify retention and clearance before translating over the supports.
The lower board is visibly retained. Raise slightly for clearance, then carry it level rearward to center above the paired base supports.
Lower the centered lower board slowly toward the support tops, keeping both end grasps closed until contact alignment can be checked.
The board appears seated across both supports. Open both grippers and withdraw outward and upward to check that the lower layer remains stable.
Lower board remains stable after release. Move outward toward the two remaining white supports while reorienting for upright block grasps.
Use the remaining supports' angled orientations for grasp alignment. Shift the wrists outward and descend to a pregrasp above each block, leaving the completed lower layer untouched.
Finish the shallow descent, close both grippers around the remaining supports, then test-lift vertically. Slight right-block yaw mismatch will be checked visually.
Both supports are visibly retained. Lift while moving inward and remove their yaw offsets so the middle supports will stand parallel on the lower board.
Center the retained middle supports symmetrically above the lower board, then begin a slow vertical descent with both grippers closed.
Set the two middle supports down gently on the lower board and open the grippers while holding position to avoid disturbing their upright placement.
Withdraw from the released middle supports and move forward/outward, beginning the inward-facing wrist rotation for the shorter board.
Both middle supports remain upright. Complete the inward-facing grasp orientation and descend above the short board's two ends, keeping the tower clear.
Descend to the shorter board's ends, close both grippers, and make a small synchronized lift to check the two-ended grasp.
Lift the shorter board level with both grippers closed, gaining clearance above the middle supports before translating it over the tower.
The short board is retained and level. Carry it rearward above the middle support pair while preserving clearance and symmetric two-arm alignment.
Lower the centered middle board slowly onto the upright middle supports, keeping both end grasps synchronized until seating can be checked.
Release the seated middle board and withdraw both wrists outward/upward. Next inspect stability before handling the remaining top pieces.
The middle layer is stable after release. Approach the small brown top board with the left arm while the right arm retreats toward home, keeping the tower clear.
Finish aligning the left gripper along the small board and descend to a pregrasp. Continue returning the right arm toward its origin without crossing workspaces.
Replan after the right-arm continuity stop with much smaller home increments. Correct the left wrist's board alignment, close, and test-lift the small top board.
The small board appears retained. Lift clear of the table and begin turning it horizontally to match the tower while keeping the right arm parked.
Carry the retained small board inward above the tower, finishing its horizontal rotation and keeping clearance over the completed middle layer.
Fine-center the brown top board over the middle board and descend slowly to its resting height; keep the left grasp closed until seating is visible.
Correct the small board slightly left for visual centering, release it onto the middle board, and withdraw upward/outward before picking the green top piece.
The brown top board is centered and stable. Move the left arm outward to a pregrasp above the remaining green piece, keeping the right arm at home.
Descend toward the green piece with a small wrist-view centering correction. Keep the gripper open until the final alignment is visible.
Fine-center the green piece between the jaws, close gently, and make a short vertical test lift to verify retention before carrying it to the tower.
The green piece is visibly retained. Lift it above the top board and align its depth before moving inward over the tower; keep the right arm parked.
Carry the upright green piece inward at constant clearance to center it over the brown top board. Check final alignment before descending.
Correct the green piece's apparent left offset and lower it slowly onto the brown board, keeping its upright orientation and closed grasp until contact is checked.
Make a small leftward centering correction, release the green piece onto the brown board, and withdraw upward/outward to inspect the completed stack.
The full stack remains upright after release. Retreat the left arm away from the tower at clearance height and begin a gradual, elbow-up return toward its origin.
Continue the left arm's curved, gradual return behind the tower, preserving elbow-up continuity. Make a small right-arm origin correction with both grippers open.
Finish the slow left-arm return to its origin and settle with both grippers open, leaving the visually stable full tower untouched.
